title: Boxing this weekend: Daniel Dubois vs. Fabio Wardley, Sebastian Fundora return - CBS Sports
description: A pair of title fights headline this weekend's action in both England and the U.S.
body:
A pair of title fights headline this weekend's action in both England and the U.S.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:35 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In May, Daniel Dubois won the WBO heavyweight championship with a stoppage win over Fabio Wardley. On Saturday, the pair will run it back in London (2 p.m. ET, DAZN PPV). That rematch highlights boxing's weekend schedule, though it's not the only world title fight on the menu.In the first meeting between Dubois and Wardley, Wardley scored knockdowns of Dubois in the first and third rounds. Despite that early success, the real story of the fight was the toughness Wardley showed across the rest of the fight, absorbing a tremendous beating from Dubois.Dubois was able to take advantage of Wardley's limited offensive approach and land crushing right hands round after round. All Wardley could do in response was go back to the well with the same looping one-two combinations that had produced the earlier knockdowns.
Wardley started boxing late in life, competing in white-collar shows from age 21 before turning professional. He found plenty of success, including late comeback knockout wins over Justis Huni and Joseph Parker in interim title fights before being promoted to full champion ahead of the Dubois fight.
Dubois came up in a more traditional fashion, working through the amateurs before turning pro. That seasoning provided the skills and knowledge that allowed Dubois to make further adjustments and become a more dynamic fighter after he tasted Wardley's power early on.Dubois has three losses in his career, all by knockout, including a pair to Oleksandr Usyk. Beyond those losses, Dubois has picked up many big wins, including over Anthony Joshua in a British megafight in 2024.Prediction: There's no reason to think the rematch plays out much differently than the first bout. That is especially true with the rematch coming so shortly after the first meeting. As mentioned, Wardley took a hellacious beating in that fight, and since then he has had to recover as much as possible and hasn't had much time to add new wrinkles to his game. Dubois is the better fighter, and as long as he can avoid a pure knockout shot, he should be able to put a hurting on Wardley again. Pick: Daniel Dubois via TKO7
Sebastian Fundora vs. Ermal HadribeajThe other big fight on Saturday takes place in Las Vegas, where Sebastian Fundora will defend his WBC junior middleweight title against Ermal Hadribeaj (8 p.m. ET, DAZN).Fundora has developed into a really good fighter after starting his career seen by many as a sideshow, with his 6-foot-6 frame towering over opponents, but a tendency to fight toe-to-toe rather than at a range that best utilized his reach. As things seemed to have been moving in the right direction, Fundora suffered a shocking knockout loss to Brian Mendoza.Fundora rebounded from the Mendoza loss with a split-decision win over Tim Tszyu that was largely attributed to Tszyu suffering a nasty cut early in the fight as a result of a Fundora elbow. Fundora erased all doubt about that win two fights later, stopping Tszyu just seven rounds into the fight.
In his most recent fight, Fundora took just six rounds to stop Keith Thurman in their March bout.Hadribeaj isn't a big-name fighter, and Fundora is far and away the best opponent he will have faced, but at 23-0-1, Hadribeaj has yet to suffer a loss. His most recent fight was a career-best win, taking a decision win over previously undefeated Bakary Samake.That said, Hadribeaj has only scored eight knockouts in his career, so he likely doesn't have the power to keep Fundora off of him as the fight wears on.
Prediction: This is set up to be little more than a showcase for Fundora. He has the better resume and the kind of physical tools that simply can't be taught. Now that Fundora better mixes in fighting at distance with his ability to stand and trade inside, he's a very big problem for the junior middleweight division. Hadribeaj doesn't figure to be the fighter who can take the belt from Fundora's waist.

title: Jaylen Waddle trade revisited: Bo Nix, Broncos struggling to integrate speedy WR - CBS Sports
description: Neither the Denver passing offense nor Waddle are playing well
body:
Neither the Denver passing offense nor Waddle are playing well
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:26 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In Bo Nix's preseason debut this year -- his first football game since breaking his ankle -- he rifled a ball to Jaylen Waddle, who had won on a vertical route up the middle of the field. Waddle caught it and sped away from his defender, a 35-yard gain. The Denver crowd erupted, even for a preseason game. This is what they had wanted so badly, the missing piece for a team that was on the doorstep of a Super Bowl berth last year.
Denver needed explosiveness. Waddle brought it in bunches. This was the start of a beautiful marriage.Or, maybe not.After another eyesore offensive performance from Denver in which Waddle was hardly involved (four catches, 24 yards), we revisit the deal this offseason that came with seemingly so much promise ... and wonder if Waddle and Nix can get on track.The tradeBroncos receive: WR Jaylen Waddle, 2026 fourth-round pick (T Kage Casey)Dolphins receive: 2026 first-round pick (used in trade up to draft CB Chris Johnson), 2026 third-round pick (WR Chris Bell), 2026 fourth-round pick (EDGE Trey Moore)The Dolphins were in the midst of a massive teardown that included the release of Tyreek Hill, Tua Tagovailoa and Bradley Chubb. Miami, 27, was neither as old as Hill or Chubb nor as costly as Tagovailoa, but Miami opted to wipe the slate as clean as possible, and Denver seemed to be the perfect home.
Denver ranked 27th in average depth of target when throwing to wide receivers last year (7.4 yards). Waddle was at 13.1.Waddle averaged 14.1 yards per catch last year; only one Denver wide receiver, Courtland Sutton was over 11.Adding the speed and explosiveness of Waddle to a group that included a big-bodied possession receiver (Sutton) and several ancillary pieces was going to unlock Nix, the Broncos thought.Bo Nix not helping Jaylen Waddle, Jaylen Waddle not helping himselfThe supposed "perfect combination" has actually been, for the most part early this season, very little combination. Through six games, Waddle has 22 catches for 228 yards and one touchdown. His 10.4 yards per reception are on pace to be his worst number since his rookie year.Jaylen Waddle this seasonOn pace for career worst?Receptions per game3.67YesReceiving yards per game38YesFirst down rate41%YesCatch rate58%YesWaddle has played a large role in that last line. He has four drops already this season after three all of last year. He came to Denver with a 6.1% career drop rate (which already wasn't great), but he is at a very bad 10.8% this year.The preseason wasn't the only false hope. After a brutal Week 1 in which pretty much everything went wrong for Denver, Waddle caught eight of 10 targets for 138 yards against the Jaguars, showing off his full skill set. He caught a 49-yarder downfield. He made catches on in-breaking routes, something he did so well in Miami. He showed off his YAC ability, and he absolutely roasted Jourdan Lewis for a crucial third-down conversion. Sean Payton talked up the need to get him the football. It seemed like all was on track.
Outside of the Jaguars game, Waddle's longest catch is 13 yards. Three of his five targets 20+ yards downfield came in the Jaguars game; the other two are an underthrow and a near-interception into double coverage. And the frustration spilled over in Week 5, when Nix checked into a run play on third and long.
Nix's passing tendencies have bordered on playing not to lose, rather than playing to win. His average throw travels 4.9 yards downfield, not only the shortest in the NFL this season but also the shortest by any quarterback through six games in the last 20 years. He simply is not even attempting to hit Waddle in the intermediate and deep areas where Waddle thrives.Furthermore, it's not as if Waddle hasn't been open. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Waddle has an average separation of 3.9 yards, the 11th-highest rate in the league and much higher than his mark last year (2.7).Remember all those fun downfield routes Waddle got against the Jaguars? Here's what his seven targeted routes looked like Thursday.
Of course, this was on a short week and just the second week since Sean Payton took playcalling duties back from Davis Webb. But there is a clear disconnect between what Waddle provides, what Nix wants to throw and what the coaching staff trusts Nix to do. One clip going around is Nix opting against firing a downfield throw to Waddle to instead throw a dump-off that gets knocked down. Like in Week 4, Waddle is not happy after the play.
It's not like the work is being funneled elsewhere. The entire passing attack is bad. Waddle leads all Broncos with 228 receiving yards and is nearly 100 yards ahead of the next-closest wide receiver (Pat Bryant, 133).At some point, Nix has to push the ball downfield. It will take a combination of his willingness and the staff scheming more downfield throws Nix is comfortable with -- his comfort level is clearly very low right now -- but this isn't close to the Waddle anyone expected. There's blame to share.It's also not worth writing off 100%. Waddle's drops are at a career-worst rate. Nix's downfield throwing is at a career-worst rate. We'd like to see more chances for Waddle on in-breaking routes -- he has just four receptions on ins, crossers, slants and posts -- and a greater willingness for Nix to throw them. The play-calling has been mixed, and Nix still doesn't look like himself. Maybe more time removed from the ankle injury, which sapped much of his offseason, will help. It's been concerning, but the season is only one-third of the way done.Too early to know about Dolphins' returnJust like it's early for Denver, it's early for Miami. In the grand scheme, it's much, much earlier, even. The Dolphins aren't likely to contend for ... a while. Assessing how they did in this trade will take ... a while.Miami and its youngsters are taking their lumps this season, as expected, but they have shown some good signs. Chris Johnson is PFF's No. 21-graded cornerback, just behind some bigger names such as Devon Witherspoon, Quinyon Mitchell and Travis Hunter.Johnson's 6.1 yards per attempt allowed as primary defender ranks 24th out of 74 defensive backs targeted at least 20 times, and his 8.6 yards per completion allowed is 11th. There is a lot to like here.It's even earlier for Chris Bell, an explosive wide receiver with borderline first-round talent who fell to the third round after a torn ACL. He has just five catches on 16 routes, but those five catches have gone for 92 yards. Again, patience is required.
Moore unfortunately suffered an ankle injury in the preseason and had to undergo surgery. He is still on IR.

title: Allisha Gray injury: Dream star 'making progress,' status for WNBA Finals unclear - CBS Sports
description: Atlanta's title chances may hinge on Gray's availability vs. Golden State
body:
Atlanta's title chances may hinge on Gray's availability vs. Golden State
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:10 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        OAKLAND, Calif. -- When the doors at the Sephora Performance Center opened on Friday morning, and media were allowed into the gym to watch the end of the Atlanta Dream's last practice ahead of the 2026 WNBA Finals, star guard Allisha Gray was running through a full-court drill with the starters. While that was a positive sign, Gray's status for Game 1 against the Golden State Valkyries on Saturday remains uncertain due to a hand injury she suffered in the semifinals. Gray, whose 19 points per game led the Dream in scoring and ranked ninth in the league, said after practice that she's still "day-to-day." Dream coach Karl Smesko said a decision on whether Gray will suit up will be made close to tip-off, which is set for 3:30 p.m. ET at Chase Center. "My hand feels good. Today in practice was really my first day of actually being able to have a full practice, go through contact and stuff like that," Gray said. "Right now I'm still day-to-day and then we're gonna see how my finger reacts to how practice went today and we'll see tomorrow."Gray, who still had the pinky and ring fingers on her left shooting hand taped together, said she doesn't think about her finger when she's on the court, and was "just so happy" to be able to "run up and down the court and be able to shoot." She added that the medical staff will ultimately make the final call on whether she'll play. 
"I think she's looking good, making progress," Smesko said. "I don't need to see anything from her. If she's able to go, we'd love for her to go."
Gray recently underwent a "minor" procedure on her left hand after she injured it during Game 1 of the semifinals against the New York Liberty. Specifics regarding her injury and the timing and extent of the procedure remain unclear. Early in that contest in Brooklyn, she deflected a pass from Sabrina Ionescu. After a short trip to the locker room, Gray returned to the game with tape on her fingers. Her first shot was a bad miss from 3-point range, so she removed the tape. In the second quarter, she made another nice defensive play on Ionescu, but aggravated the injury in the process and has not played since. 
Despite Gray's absence, the Dream swept the Liberty in three games to advance to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013. 
Dream's title chances may hinge on Gray's availability"Allisha's one of the best players in the W," Dream coach Karl Smesko said Tuesday. "To advance and beat a great New York team basically without her, except for 10 minutes of one game, is a testament to everybody else raising their game. But it would be great to have her back for the Finals. She's just somebody that, offensively, is really hard to stop, and then she makes defensive plays. She's just an all-around great player."
        
            
                2026 WNBA playoffs bracket: WNBA Finals schedule tweaked so Dream can use larger venue
                
                    Lindsay Gibbs                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The Dream's ability to beat the Valkyries and win the first championship in franchise history may hinge on Gray's availability. Jordin Canada, DeWanna Bonner and Isobel Borlase were spectacular in the semifinals against the Liberty, but it's a big ask for them to repeat these performances:
Canada had three of the five-highest playoff scoring performances of her career against the Liberty, and averaged 22.3 points on 62.2/61.5/100 shooting splits -- up from 11.6 points on 43.1/29.2/78.2 shooting in the regular season. Bonner went for 15.3 points and 8.3 rebounds on 50/46.7/80 shooting splits, up from 10.4 points and six rebounds on 40.2/27.9/84.3 shooting between the Phoenix Mercury and Dream in the regular season. And Borlase, who only had six double-digit scoring games in the regular season, came off the bench to chip in 11 points in Game 2 and 10 points in Game 3 while shooting 9 of 15, including 3 of 6 from 3-point range. The Valkyries have the best defense in the league by a wide margin, and just shut down A'ja Wilson and Jackie Young in a sweep of the Las Vegas Aces. Even acknowledging the Valkyries' own issues on offense, it's hard to imagine how the Dream would be able to score enough points to beat them without Gray. While Gray will clearly not be 100% if she suits up, having an All-WNBA-caliber talent on the floor that the Valkyries have to respect would make life far easier for the Dream.

title: Dream pairing: How Angel Reese and her new team brought out the best in each other to reach the WNBA Finals - CBS Sports
description: Reese, who could be the first star of her generation to win a WNBA title, has changed her game with the Dream
body:
Reese, who could be the first star of her generation to win a WNBA title, has changed her game with the Dream
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:11 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream currently sit just four games away from being crowned WNBA champions. It would be a franchise-first for the Dream, who joined the WNBA in 2008, and make Reese the first star of her generation to lead her team to a title. Things looked very different for both parties not so long ago.This time last year, then-Chicago Sky forward Angel Reese was sitting at home on her couch, watching the Finals from afar after missing the postseason in her first two years in the league. About 700 miles south in Atlanta, the Dream were in soul-searching mode after the winningest regular season in Dream history ended in a postseason flameout.Reese's two years in Chicago had been marked by phenomenal individual play on the court and a sizeable economic impact to the franchise and community, both of which were often overshadowed by poor team play, perplexing roster decisions, coaching instability and front-office mismanagement. By the end of the 2025 season, when Reese gave an ill-advised on-the-record interview to the Chicago Tribune that threw shade on teammates and leadership (and the Sky responded by suspending her for half of a game), it was clear that the two sides were no longer bringing out the best in one another.
        
            
                2026 WNBA Finals predictions: Expert picks for Valkyries vs. Dream as each team seeks first title
                
                    Lindsay Gibbs                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Meanwhile, the Dream's first year under new head coach Karl Smesko had resulted in 15 more wins than their 2024 campaign and a No. 3 seed and home-court advantage in the playoffs, but the end result was the same as it had been the two years prior: A first-round loss, this time at the hands of an injury-plagued Indiana Fever team. The Dream had All-Stars, but no superstars; they were tough, but lacked a competitive fire; they had a strong culture and core, but did not know how to harness any of that when it mattered the most. 
So, when Reese was traded from the Chicago Sky to the Atlanta Dream on April 6, the match immediately made sense. Reese needed a fresh start, a steady organization and a talented roster. The Dream needed a winner and a fighter -- not to mention one of the best rebounders and defenders in the game."It felt like the right situation for me, and I felt like I was able to come here and help the team in any way I could. Coaches and a GM that really believe in me was something I was really, really wanting after my first two years," Reese said in her introductory press conference.How the Dream made Reese betterBut what turned the pairing from sensible to sensational was what came next. Smesko knew that the skillset Reese came to town with would make the Dream better instantly. But she lacked in one area that Smesko is famous for valuing -- the ability to shoot from the 3-point line. Due to the condensed offseason schedule, a consequence of the late arrival of the new CBA, Smesko didn't have time to feel Reese out, ease her into his system, to see first-hand if the rumors that had always followed her about being a diva or too distracted by off-court endeavors were true. He had to decide right away how much change she could handle. And so Smesko did what he's always done -- he decided to coach Reese hard. And Reese let him.
Right away, he set out to change her shooting motion and push her to take more shots from the 3-point line. He told her that if she made one more 3-pointer every 25 shots, even that would make a difference in how teams guarded her. And then he put her under duress. There was no time for this growth to happen in private; the season would be starting in a few weeks. She was going to have to try new things, and fail at them, in front of everyone."It's really hard for me to not want to rush success. And Karl told me how patient I had to be with it," Reese recalled after the semifinals, when asked about her improvements from outside the arch.Just a couple of days into training camp, in a new city on a new team with new eyes tracking her every move, the players were doing a 3-point drill when Smesko stopped practice and told Reese that she had to make two 3-pointers in a row, in front of everyone, before practice resumed. Everyone had to stop what they were doing and watch Reese try to succeed at the only part of basketball she hadn't yet mastered. 
"I was upset with him that day for sure because I didn't want to let the team down. I didn't want to feel embarrassed of how long it could have took me to make them," she said. "I think you have to understand -- you're at the W level, and we changed her shot, like, completely, and then we asked her to do it in games. And we talked about it," Smesko said. "We said, 'Before the All Star break, you're still going to shoot these open threes. This is how we want you to shoot it. It's not going to be a good percentage. After the All Star break, it's going to start to get better. By the time we get to the end of the season, it'll start to feel really comfortable.'"So you had to go through all those growing pains, and do that in front of everybody. That's the reason why I had her do it in front of her teammates. You're going to have to get comfortable shooting this ball in front of people, and it's brand new to you. It's not comfortable to you."
Smesko was right about the timeline. Before the All-Star break, Reese shot 12% on 3-pointers. After All-Star break, that improved to 25%. In the playoffs? It has improved to 38.5% and been a huge reason why the Dream have not yet lost a game in this postseason."Now it's so easy. My confidence is through the roof," Reese said. "When I shoot them, it just feels like practice. You have those tough times, and you have those tough conversations. But it's a coach that really believes in you, and he knows he knows what's best. And I'm really thankful for him for being able to help me with my career and help me be better for the team. Because I don't think I would be in this situation and thriving as I am individually without him."It won't be easy vs. ValksThe Dream have a tall task ahead of them this series. The Valkyries have home-court advantage, so Reese and co. will start the series on the road in San Francisco on Saturday, and the best defense in the league. But with Reese, the Dream have found their edge and are on a 10-game winning streak. During that span, they've won in blowouts and in tight games, in shootouts and in scrap-fests. And with the Dream, Reese has found the best basketball of her young career, and a place where she can showcase all of her talents and even add some to the mix. The two were a perfect fit, and have worked together to become even greater than the sum of their parts. 
"Just knowing I belong here," Reese said, when asked why she's flourished in Atlanta. "Knowing coming to Atlanta, how much I wanted to help this team and do whatever it takes, not just to get out of the first round, not to just to get out the semis, but to make it to the Finals and win a championship. And the job is not done. We're definitely happy about where we are right now, but we're not satisfied."

title: Washington QB Demond Williams Jr. to miss game vs. Purdue with rib injury - CBS Sports
description: Junior backup signal caller Elijah Brown will get the start for the Huskies as they look to correct their offenis
body:
Junior backup signal caller Elijah Brown will get the start for the Huskies as they look to correct their offenisve woes against the Boilermakers
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:25 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With star quarterback Demond Williams Jr. sidelined with a rib injury, junior Elijah Brown will start for Washington against Purdue on Friday night.It's already been a tough season for the Huskies, but this development won't make it any easier. Washington is still looking for its first win in Big Ten play, and that task just got a little more difficult.Brown, a former four-star recruit out of California, played the first two seasons of his career at Stanford before transferring to Washington in the offseason. Brown saw a little action at Stanford and started in a couple of games last season, most notably in a win over Cal and a loss to North Carolina.In nine career appearances with the Cardinal, Brown completed 58.3 percent of his passes for 1,103 yards, six touchdowns and five interceptions. Brown has played in mop-up duty a few times in his first season at Washington, resulting in 276 yards, four touchdowns and zero interceptions on 71.4 percent passing.
Washington needs Brown to spark the passing game because that's been the only way the offense has moved the ball this season. The Huskies rank 16th in the Big Ten with 26.2 points per game, and a pitiful run game has a lot to do with that.Bad news for a struggling offenseAlthough Williams has been somewhat disappointing in 2026, he's still done enough to make plays and put the ball in the end zone on a number of occasions. In other words, Williams has found a way to make it work here and there.The same can't be said for the running game, which has been anemic. The Huskies average just 90.3 rushing yards per game, which ranks 135th out of 138 teams nationall. They also rank 106th in yards per rush (4.06) and rushing success rate (39.7 percent).
That's a bad recipe for a team starting an unproven quarterback on the road in conference play, although there is some hope that Brown has what it takes to lead the offense efficiently.After Williams got hurt against Iowa last week, Brown relatively well in relief. In fact, he started the second half 14-of-16 while leading two straight touchdown drives against the Hawkeyes defense."Just trusting in the process," Brown said of his performance against Iowa. "Just trusting in the coach's plans. I feel like they prepared us very well. That's pretty much it."
Perhaps Brown has taken big strides in his first year at Washington. That would be great, but what if he hasn't? Didn't Dylan Raiola look great against USC when he took over for an injured Dante Moore. One week later, he was benched against UCLA.If Brown does struggle, Washington will go from one-dimensional to zero-dimensional on offense, and even a subpar defense like Purdue's could slow down the Huskies. In that case, Jedd Fisch and and his team would be on their way to a 3-4 record while remaining winless in Big Ten play.

title: Michigan vs. Penn State prediction, picks, odds, spread, where to watch live - CBS Sports
description: Michigan and Penn State both enter Saturday's contest looking to snap losing streaks
body:
Michigan and Penn State both enter Saturday's contest looking to snap losing streaks
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:26 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Penn State and Michigan will meet on Saturday in a matchup between two teams already in desperation mode midway through the season. Both began the 2026 season hopeful for the future with a new coach in charge. Six weeks into the season, that hope and optimism have turned into doom and gloom for both programs that enter Week 7 on losing streaks in Big Ten play. The Wolverines began the season with a controversial win before beating Oklahoma in Week 2 for what seemed, at the time, like Kyle Whittingham's first signature win in Ann Arbor. However, successive losses to Iowa and Minnesota, where the offense has looked inept, have raised the temperature under Whittingham just five games into his tenure. The Nittany Lions had a lengthy coaching search before finally bringing in Matt Campbell from Iowa State, and Penn State fans expected a swift return to Big Ten contention. Three consecutive losses to open conference play have already raised questions about Campbell's fit in State College, and he finds himself in desperation mode heading on the road into a hostile environment. 
For years, Penn State vs. Michigan was one of the biggest games of the year in the old Big Ten East. This year, what it lacks in intrigue regarding the College Football Playoff race, it makes up for in what it will tell us about the trajectory of two traditional Big Ten powers. The winner will be able to let out a sigh of relief, while the loser will be staring down a fight just to make it to a bowl game in 2026.   Michigan vs. Penn State: Need to know  Bryce Underwood as a runner: In Michigan's biggest win of the season against Oklahoma, it was Underwood running the ball that was the difference for the Wolverines. He carried the ball 18 times for 87 yards and one touchdown, which was by far his most productive rushing game of the season. The Penn State defense has struggled this season, and both Aidan Chiles and Colton Joseph have rushed for touchdowns against them for Northwestern and Wisconsin. Throwing the ball consistently hasn't been a strength of the Michigan offense, and in a game they desperately need, look for the Wolverines to try and take advantage of Underwood as a runner at times -- especially in red zone opportunities. Can Penn State create explosive plays?: Moving the ball on Michigan's defense consistently is a difficult task, and in both of their losses, it was explosives that led to scores for Minnesota and Iowa. Penn State's offense ranks in the middle of the pack in explosive plays this season, but has not been as dynamic since Koby Howard's injury took away their top downfield threat. If the Nittany Lions are going to score against Michigan, they have to find a way to produce some explosive plays. That doesn't always have to mean on offense. Iowa's first touchdown against Michigan came on a punt return. Minnesota forced three turnovers that led to 13 of their 20 points. Penn State will need a handful of chunk plays from the offense and to create some havoc on defense and special teams if they're going to win this game. 
Special teams, special teams, special teams: This is the kind of game where special teams matter a bit more than usual -- which is to say, this is going to be Big Ten football heritage on display. The punters on both sides need to be sharp and avoid handing the opponent a short field. With points at a premium, field goal opportunities will need to be converted. And with two offenses that can get stuck in the mud, a big return could swing this game one way or the other. Special teams has not been the strength of the Wolverines this season, as they rank 89th in special teams SP+, while Penn State is in the middle of the pack (49th). The team that wins the special teams battle will gain a considerable advantage, and for underdog Penn State in particular, being sharp in the third phase is a must to win on the road. Where to watch Michigan vs. Penn State live  Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time: 3:30 p.m. ET  Location: Michigan Stadium -- Ann Arbor, MichiganTV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com, CBS Sports App  Streaming on Paramount+ Premium
  Michigan vs. Penn State prediction, picks  There is a "stoppable force vs. movable object" situation happening here with the Michigan offense against the Penn State defense, but I'm banking on the home team dictating the tempo here in a classic Big Ten rock fight. Michigan games have finished with fewer than 40 total points four times in five games -- with the lone exception being against lowly UTEP -- and even against a leaky Nittany Lions defense, it's hard to see this Michigan offense being overly explosive. First place and a potential NWSL Shield clinch are on the line at Audi Field, while Washington fight to lock down a playoff spot in the latest chapter of their fierce rivalry

        It's the best time of the year in NWSL, the playoff push. With just a few games left in the 2026 regular season and the NWSL Shield still up for grabs, every game from here on out feels like a must-win. But, add rivalry to the mix, and the stakes get a little higher.Every great rivalry has iconic moments, and Gotham FC and Washington Spirit have already racked up several in recent years. Washington Spirit won a triumphant penalty shootout at Audi Field in the 2024 NWSL semifinals, and Gotham FC won last year's NWSL Championship game.Earlier this season, Gotham took home bragging rights with a narrow 1-0 win for the first-ever victory at MLB's Citi Field in front of 42,175 fans.
The two teams will meet in a final regular-season fixture, just weeks before the NWSL playoffs begin. But both sides have stakes in the match. Gotham FC already claimed a postseason spot, are in first place, are leading the NWSL Shield race, and can potentially lift the shield. Meanwhile, the Spirit are in third place, still in contention for the shield, and chasing a playoff clinch.
However, both rosters face uncertainty ahead of the game. Injury concerns and cohesion struggles loom, and with the playoffs so close, gamesmanship could flare in a rivalry that's already typically cagey.How to watch Washington Spirit vs. Gotham FC, oddsDate: Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time: 12:30 p.m. ETLocation: Audi Field -- Washington, D.C.TV: CBS Odds: Washington Spirit +160; Draw +230; NJ/NJ Gotham +155Injury concerns for Gotham FCGotham FC have been on an impressive run of form since the league returned following a summer break for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, with only two losses since July 4. With an unbeaten run through August and more wins in September, the East Coast club has held on firmly to first place. 
Equally impressive has been the club's ability to navigate changes across the sidelines and the roster. Head coach Juan Carlos Amoros and his family welcomed a new baby, and he took parental leave back in July."I'm incredibly grateful to everyone at Gotham FC for supporting us unconditionally while we were deciding to take this step," Amoros said in the summer. "This is a personal decision for our family, but I also recognize the visibility that comes with my role. When fathers take parental leave, particularly men in leadership positions, it helps normalize an important principle: Caring for children is a shared responsibility between parents. I need to be there for my family."Between then-acting head coach Shaun Harris and Amoros, the club's record was ten wins, three draws, and two losses through September, and they also had to manage the roster as injuries piled up, with a season-ending torn patellar tendon for Emily Sonnett and a brief concussion precaution for Rose Lavelle. 
The injury list is still growing ahead of Saturday's big game. Rookie Jordynn Dudley's impressive campaign was cut short with a foot fracture, and while on international duty, Brazilian defender Brunhina tore her ACL. Both players are on the season-ending injury list ahead of the weekend. Jaedyn Shaw was recently called up to join USWNT camps with the U23 side, though she was sent home early as a precaution following a minor injury. She is currently day-to-day and expected to be available for Saturday's game against the Spirit.The recent international window may have added minutes for players on national teams; it may have come at a good time for others ahead of a potential NWSL Shield clinch scenario. One of Gotham's strengths this season has been a deep bench that has played together for a few seasons, while rookies stepped up and new additions like Australian international Sam Kerr have slotted in fairly seamlessly following the departure of Esther Gonzalez.
The recent acquisition of Spain defender Leila Ouahabi could mean another tactical shift for Midge Purce, who could play more of an attacking role along the front line, while Ouahabi shifts into a natural position at outside back.Cohesion struggles for Washington SpiritThe Spirit's second half of the season has been more split than Gotham. With eight wins, six losses, and one draw since July, the group has struggled to keep pace for the NWSL Shield, but looks primed for another postseason appearance. Inconsistency in results isn't uncommon in a long NWSL season, and the Spirit shook off a four-game winless streak in August to finally pick up a trio of wins across five matches in September. Roster churn could also help explain some of the unevenness.
Beyond preseason movement, including key midfield departures Croix Bethune (Kansas City Current) and Narumi Miura (Utah Royals) to other playoff-contending teams at the start of the season, the club has made plenty of mid- to late-season roster shakeups. Cameroonian midfielder Monique Ngock and Algerian midfielder Mélissa Bethi joined after the Women's Africa Cup of Nations, and the club recently signed Tanzanian national team forward Clara Luvanga. Mexico international Rebecal Bernal, with 20 appearances for the Spirit this season, joined Manchester United in September. Losing a regular from the squad in the middle of a Shield chase left little time for the defense or midfield to readjust, especially with Leicy Santos out for an extended injury absence. Though there might finally be some light at the end of the long absence tunnel.
Both Andi Sullivan and Ashley Hatch returned to the roster following maternity leave midseason and earned match minutes, and head coach Adrian Gonzalez said in a recent pregame press conference that Santos will be available for selection against Gotham.It's a sign that maybe the international break arrived at a good time for the club's recent signings and injured players. The franchise is investing in international talent, and that's positive for the present and future, but chemistry rarely arrives the moment a new deal is signed. Now that everyone has had a handful of games to get acclimated and a brief international break in the schedule, the Spirit can look ahead to managing the three games remaining in front of them, but first is a high-stakes game against Gotham.What's at stakeThere's plenty to play for on Saturday. Gotham is chasing a prize it has never won. With two NWSL Championships, a Concacaf title, and a recent NWSL Challenge Cup, the title of best team in the league has eluded them. They have a chance to hoist the Shield with a road win over one of their oldest rivals, with help from a North Carolina Courage win.
"There's not a lot of direct talk about it because we all understand that what we're doing every day and every week is what leads to that. So while it's an ultimate goal that we've set from the beginning of preseason, we have a good understanding that thinking about that goal is not necessarily what's going to get you there. It's what you're doing every day at training; it's what you're doing on the weekend playing these games," said Gotham defender Tierna Davidson before the international break."That's really what we're focused on, knowing in the back of our minds that that's what we're working towards together. I also think too, sometimes if you talk about something too much, you forget what's right in front of you. And that's important that we continue to focus on what's in front of us ... ultimately, as a team, we understand that there are short-term goals, midterm goals, long-term goals, but we can accomplish all of that together without having to compromise in any way," she said.The Spirit have the math on their side in the Shield race, but they must beat Gotham and win their remaining games (nine points) to have a shot.
Beyond the shield, there is playoff positioning on the line for both sides. Even if Gotham stumble in their remaining games, the pride of playing for a home playoff is there. Teams that place first through fourth could potentially host up to two home games. Gotham has already clinched a postseason spot, and the Spirit can also cement another postseason berth with a win, or help from positive results by San Diego, Bay FC, or Chicago.

title: Can the Broncos win a Super Bowl with Bo Nix? His stats tell a troubling story - CBS Sports
description: Bo Nix is 28-12 through his first 40 NFL starts, more victories than John Elway and Peyton Manning had over that same stretch. Among act
body:
Bo Nix is 28-12 through his first 40 NFL starts, more victories than John Elway and Peyton Manning had over that same stretch. Among active quarterbacks, only Patrick Mahomes and Lamar Jackson had better records at this point in their careers.There's just one problem: Nix is directing one of the NFL's least productive offenses, and his individual numbers are getting worse. So what exactly should we make of all that success?Thursday night's 17-14 overtime victory against Seattle might have been the most extreme example yet. Denver managed 168 yards of offense, averaged 2.9 yards per play and gained a grand total of 38 yards on 25 plays after halftime. Nix finished with 107 passing yards, averaging exactly four yards per attempt.Former NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick wasn't nearly as forgiving. During Amazon's postgame show, he ripped Nix's performance, saying, "He's not playing competitive football right now," and later calling it "almost disrespectful to the quarterback position." 
So, yeah … the Broncos improved to 4-2 and extended their streak of one-score victories to 14 games. Their defense dominated for long stretches, forcing turnovers and capitalizing on Seattle's mistakes. And it's not a stretch to suggest they accomplished all this in spite of, not because of Bo Nix.Denver has a defense capable of carrying this team to the Super Bowl. But if Nix can't give the Broncos more than he has through the first six games, none of that matters. Put more bluntly: How much longer are they willing to wait for him to figure it out?What Nix's first 39 starts actually tell usIt's easy to look at Nix's 2026 numbers, throw your hands up and conclude that he's suddenly fallen apart. The third-year quarterback has undoubtedly gotten worse this season, but some of the problems have been there all along.
Nix threw 29 touchdowns and 12 interceptions as a rookie in 2024 and helped Denver reach the playoffs. He followed that with another winning season, and through his first 39 starts, he'd thrown 60 touchdowns, completed 64.2% of his passes and piled up 8,648 passing yards.Those aren't bad numbers, and Nix, at times, has looked comfortable running Sean Payton's offense. Enough to give Denver reason to believe it had found its long-term answer. But look a little deeper, and the picture starts to change.Nix's efficiency -- how consistently he moves the ball, creates big plays and avoids negative ones -- doesn't quite match his impressive record, according to TruMedia. To put that into perspective, we compared him to a sample of 74 other quarterbacks drafted since 2008, looking at how each performed through his first 39 starts over his first three NFL seasons.
NixRankEPA/dropback+0.0530thSuccess rate43.4%40thYards/attempt6.459thAdjusted yards/attempt7.073rdExplosive plays/dropback7.4%45thSack rate3.7%1stPressure-to-sack rate11.2%75th (best)Nix excelled at avoiding sacks, getting the ball out quickly and keeping Denver out of trouble. But there was a tradeoff: He wasn't making nearly enough big plays through the air, and his 6.4 yards per attempt ranked 59th among the 75 quarterbacks in our sample.In other words, Nix was good at avoiding mistakes, but not nearly as good at making plays that could change a game. And through six games in 2026, even that formula has started to fall apart.The warning signs are getting harder to ignoreNix isn't just throwing shorter passes. He's taking fewer chances downfield, making more turnover-worthy plays and struggling to move the offense. And when he does drop back, he's getting less out of those opportunities than at any point in his career.Consider how his numbers have changed since his rookie season.202420252026Yards/attempt6.76.45.6EPA/dropback+0.05+0.11-0.12Average depth of target7.88.06.3Big-time throw rate3.5%4.8%2.4%Turnover-worthy play rate1.9%2.8%5.0%Accuracy percentage76.7%75.6%74.7%Pressure-to-sack rate13.3%10.1%10.1%There was genuine progress in 2025. Nix's EPA per dropback increased, his big-time throw rate improved and he did a better job of avoiding sacks when pressured. That's meaningful, and it offers at least some evidence that he was improving.But through six games in 2026, those gains have largely disappeared. His big-time throw rate has been cut in half, his turnover-worthy play rate has nearly doubled from last season and his EPA per dropback has turned negative.And while his accuracy rate has remained stable, he's generating fewer first downs, explosive plays and touchdowns. And he's putting the ball in harm's way more often.There's also the ankle injury to consider. Nix underwent surgery after fracturing his right ankle in January's playoff win over Buffalo, but he has repeatedly insisted he's fully healthy. Asked directly after Denver's Week 4 loss to San Francisco whether the injury was affecting his play, he offered a one-word answer: "No." It's certainly fair to wonder, based on what we've all witnessed this season, if that's not entirely true.  There's also the fact that Payton has commandeered play-calling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb, hoping to jump-start an offense that had struggled through its first four games.So far, it hasn't helped. Denver managed just 224 yards against the Chargers in Week 5 and 168 against Seattle, and the Broncos now rank 31st in yards per game and last in yards per play. Payton helped Nix develop over his first two seasons, but the last two weeks have only raised more questions about whether he'll ever become the quarterback Denver envisioned when they drafted him.How Nix compares to the other QBs in that 2024 draft classNix was the 12th overall pick, and the sixth quarterback taken in the 2024 NFL Draft, behind Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels, Drake Maye, Michael Penix Jr. and JJ McCarthy.Some two-and-a-half seasons later, how does Nix stack up against his classmates? Maye helped lead the Patriots to the Super Bowl in Year 2, while Daniels took Washington to the NFC Championship Game as a rookie. Williams made significant strides under Ben Johnson in 2025, leading Chicago to a division title and a playoff victory, and Penix has been surprisingly impressive this season. Even with injuries complicating the comparisons, there's enough evidence to suggest every quarterback in this class not named Nix or McCarthy is developing into the player their teams envisioned. 2024 first-round QB class: NFL passing production, 2024-26QuarterbackGamesYPAEPA/dropbackTD-INTDrake Maye358.1+0.1754-25Jayden Daniels277.1+0.1436-12Michael Penix Jr.177.6+0.1115-7Bo Nix406.4+0.0560-26Caleb Williams366.7+0.0549-14J.J. McCarthy106.7-0.1011-12Nix has started more games than anyone in the group, and unlike several of his classmates, he's had the same coach and offensive system since arriving in the NFL. That stability should have helped his development, and for a while, it appeared to. But through six games in '26, Nix is heading in the wrong direction.That doesn't mean Denver should give up and move on. But after 40 starts, his struggles raise a bigger question: How much longer should the Broncos expect to wait for a breakthrough?What history says about young QBs who struggle this longSo what happens to quarterbacks whose numbers look like Nix's after some 40 starts? Do they figure it out, or is three seasons enough to know what you have?The good news for Denver is that some quarterbacks do turn things around. The bad news? Most don't suddenly become stars. There's a big difference between improving enough to keep your job and becoming the guy who can carry a team to the Super Bowl.We used TruMedia data to look at 24 quarterbacks whose early-career efficiency resembled Nix's, then compared their first 39 starts with their next 21. Nine improved their EPA per dropback by at least 0.05. But just four reached +0.10 or better, and as it turns out, even that didn't guarantee long-term success.What happened to quarterbacks who started their careers like Bo Nix?QuarterbackFirst 39 startsStarts 40-60Starts 61-80Josh Allen+0.06+0.15+0.21Dak Prescott+0.06+0.18+0.12Tua Tagovailoa+0.05+0.17-0.02Jared Goff+0.06+0.10-0.10Baker Mayfield+0.01+0.06-0.08Derek Carr0.00+0.06-0.02Andy Dalton+0.01+0.03+0.15Blake Bortles-0.03+0.05-0.09Mitchell Trubisky+0.01-0.02—Mark Sanchez0.00-0.13—Josh Allen and Dak Prescott give Denver some hope. Both started with numbers similar to Nix's, took major steps forward over their next 21 starts and continued to produce at a high level over the following 20 games. Andy Dalton, stylistically a much closer comp to Nix than Allen or Prescott, needed a little longer, making his biggest leap between starts 61 and 80.Others followed a different path. Tua Tagovailoa, Jared Goff and Baker Mayfield initially improved, only to see their numbers fall off during the next 20 starts. Derek Carr and Blake Bortles also made gains before regressing, while Mitch Trubisky and Mark Sanchez, both top-5 picks in their respective draft classes, never made much progress. Of course, Goff and Mayfield eventually turned their careers around, which shows that development is rarely linear.And there's another catch: Our comparison only includes quarterbacks who had at least 300 dropbacks after their first 39 starts. Some struggling quarterbacks never got that opportunity because their teams moved on. Put another way: The odds of a turnaround may be even worse than our numbers suggest.So where does that leave Nix? He's done enough to keep his starting job for now, but his performance has gotten worse in Year 3.  History offers some hope that he can still figure things out, but it also gives Payton and general manager George Paton good reason to wonder how much longer they should wait.How much longer can Denver afford to wait?Under ordinary circumstances, the answer might be straightforward. Nix is still young. He's won a lot of games, and the Broncos have invested heavily in his development. Give him more time and see where things go.But Denver isn't in an ordinary situation.
The Broncos have a defense capable of keeping them in every game. They have a coach who has already won a Super Bowl, and they've built a team that doesn't need its quarterback to throw for 350 yards every week.What they need is an offense that can consistently move the ball. Right now, it's nonexistent.And that's what makes the coming offseason potentially so important. Nix is under contract through 2027, with Denver holding a fifth-year option for 2028. The Broncos don't have to decide his long-term future just yet, but they can't afford to waste a championship-caliber defense waiting for him to develop.There's no guarantee this defense will be this dominant in 2027, never mind 2-3 years down the road; injuries happen, contracts expire, players and units regress, and championship windows can slam shut.That doesn't mean Denver needs to move on from Nix, but they would be foolish not to start considering other options. Nix can change the conversation over the next few months. But Payton and Paton also need to prepare for the possibility that the quarterback they have isn't the one they need to win a Super Bowl.That could mean using a 2027 draft pick on a quarterback or bringing in legitimate veteran competition. Neither would necessarily mean giving up on Nix – J.J. McCarthy might like a word, I know. Either way,  it would give Denver another option if his struggles continue.(By the way, I've documented – extensively, some might say – Arch Manning's struggles this season for Texas. He wasn't a first-round pick in my latest mock draft, or the latest mock draft we did on the "With the First Pick" podcast … that said, imagine if Payton got his hands on him. Just something to think about.)The Broncos have spent two-plus seasons waiting for Nix to grow into a franchise quarterback. They can afford to give him more time, but they can't afford to squander a Super Bowl window hoping for a breakthrough that may never come.

The Crimson Tide will be looking to avoid losing consecutive regular season games for the first time since 2007, while the Volunteers will be seeking to snap a four-game home losing streak against ranked opponents.Alabama (5-1, 3-1 SEC) took a 20-17 home loss to Georgia last week, which leaves the Crimson Tide with a dwindling margin for error entering the second half of their schedule. Tennessee (5-1, 2-1) is coming off an ugly 24-17 win at Arkansas in need of the resume boost that would come with knocking off Alabama.While Tennessee's defense is thriving midway through the season, facing Alabama will be its toughest test yet. Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell leads the league in passing yards with 1,599 and brings game-changing mobility. Though Alabama star receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams is expected to miss the game due to injury, Bama's offense will still pack a punch that tests Tennessee's secondary.The Volunteers counter with the nation's No. 15 rushing offense and a languishing passing attack that will need to get better if they are going to pull an upset that would reverberate through the SEC and beyond. With blowout road wins over quality foes Kentucky and Mississippi State already in hand, the Tide will look to keep rolling on the road with their first win in Knoxville since 2020.
  Alabama vs. Tennessee: Need to know  Neyland blues: The last time Tennessee beat a ranked team at Neyland Stadium was in 2024, when it edged No. 7 Alabama 24-17. The Vols finished 0-3 at home against ranked opponents last season and fell 20-17 to Texas in Week 4, extending their home losing streak against ranked opponents to four games. But something will have to give as the Crimson Tide have dropped two straight inside Neyland Stadium. Whichever team is smoking, the traditional postgame victory cigars will hit a little different this time.Tennessee's QB question: Tennessee sophomore quarterback George MacIntyre made his first career start last week in the Volunteers' 24-17 win at Arkansas, stepping in for injured and underperforming freshman Faizon Brandon. Now the question is how long the Volunteers will stick with MacIntyre, who completed 18 of 29 passes for 247 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions against the Razorbacks. Regardless of who gets the nod against Alabama, the Crimson Tide's priority will be to slow down the SEC's second-leading rusher, DeSean Bishop, and to make Tennessee's fledgling passing attack prove that it can deliver.Playoff implications: With a win, Alabama will have an 87.7% chance of reaching the College Football Playoff, according to the CBS Sports College Football Playoff Forecaster. A loss would drop that mark to 52.9% and crush Alabama's margin for error. Because the Crimson Tide's strength of schedule lags behind others in the SEC, its case for inclusion as a three-loss team would be shaky. description: Both players will become eligible for Week 7, although their teams must determine whether they are ready to play
body:
Both players will become eligible for Week 7, although their teams must determine whether they are ready to play
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:21 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The league announced two players will be removed from the NFL's Commissioner Exempt list in the coming days. Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper will be removed on Friday, and Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs on Monday.Cooper is eligible to play in Denver's Week 7 game against the Arizona Cardinals, and Jacobs is expected to be eligible to play in Green Bay's Week 7 game against the Detroit Lions, according to ESPN. "The league's review of both the Josh Jacobs and Jonathon Cooper situations 'remains ongoing' and is not affected by the change to either player's status," the report states. Players on the commissioner's exempt list continue to be paid. If the NFL later suspends either player, the league could credit the games missed on the exempt list toward the suspension and seek repayment of salary earned during that period. Being on the list means players cannot attend practice or games. 
Cooper was dismissed from minicamp and was placed on the list ahead of the season following two arrests involving an alleged domestic violence incident with his ex-girlfriend in June. He faces five charges, including second-degree felony assault. His trial was moved from mid-November to early March.Cooper has spent his entire career thus far with the Broncos, who drafted him in the seventh round of the 2021 NFL Draft. Jacobs was charged with two misdemeanors, battery and damage to property, from an arrest in May. Jacobs filed an action seeking to prevent the public release of evidence related to the case, including alleged video of the incident. Jacobs' attorney released a statement saying he "accepts responsibility for his actions" and says he is "excited to get back on the field with his teammates."
Jacobs signed a four-year, $48 million deal with the Packers heading into the 2024 season and he is now in his third year with the team. The All-Pro was selected by the Las Vegas Raiders at No. 24 overall in the 2019 NFL Draft.In his absence, RB Marshawn Lloyd has led the team with just 112 rushing yards and two touchdowns. Kaleb Johnson is second on the team with 106 yards. While both players will be eligible to return in Week 7, that decision is ultimately up to the coaches and players involved.

title: Nick Saban opposes 24-team College Football Playoff expansion - CBS Sports
description: The former Alabama coach is okay with postseason changes, but wants something different
body:
The former Alabama coach is okay with postseason changes, but wants something different
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:28 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The College Football Playoff is in the process of expanding to 24 teams starting in the 2027 season, much to the chagrin of Nick Saban, who says doubling the number of teams in the current bracket is far too many."I would be for 16 (teams) – I think that would be a good compromise," Saban said Friday on ESPN. "I would be for keeping conference championship games as maybe a play-in for the 16? Which, now, you have 20 teams that have hope. But I don't think there's much support for that. I don't think anybody really likes that."The new format is expected to feature a "19+4+1" model with 19 at-large bids, four reserved for Power Four champions and one for the highest-rated Group of Six champ. Theoretically, that would mean almost every team in the final top 25 rankings would play in the playoff.That also means the likely end of conference championship games. For the SEC, an expanded bracket to 24 teams would need to offset the league's financial losses from losing its title game, which is estimated around $100 million.
"The bottom line is money. That's the bottom line," Saban said "You explained it. Universities need it because of the way we're spending more now for players. There's still a cost to having Olympic sports, which are important, I think to be able to keep and give people opportunities to compete. And how do we do that?"
CBS Sports' Brandon Marcello reported this week the CFP could offer an additional $320 million on top of the current contract.Previously, decision-makers in the Big Ten and the SEC were at a stalemate over future CFP formats. The Big Ten prefers a 24-team field with multiple automatic qualifiers per conference, while the SEC preferred a 16-team "5+11" format. That has since changed according to SEC commissioner Greg Sankey, who said this week at the league's basketball media days a decision on expansion was coming "sooner rather than later" in the coming weeks.
"Attitudes change over time and perspectives change, and so we'll see where that leads us from a final decision standpoint," Sankey said, via The Athletic. "I think in general, we have achieved some of the progress we've expected on scheduling commitments. We'll see if we can finalize those across the nation."

title: Mike Macdonald says Seahawks will not bench Sam Darnold for Drew Lock - CBS Sports
description: Darnold has thrown an NFL-high seven interceptions, but Macdonald stands behind his starter

Darnold has thrown an NFL-high seven interceptions, but Macdonald stands behind his starter

                    at
    1:47 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It hasn't been the best season for Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold. He suffered a gluteal injury during the team's season opener and has struggled quite a bit since returning from it. Darnold has completed only 60.4% of his passes at an average of just 6.9 yards per attempt, and he's thrown for seven touchdowns against an NFL-high seven interceptions. He seemingly hit a nadir on Thursday night against the Broncos, completing 52.9% of his passes at 5.5 yards per attempt and throwing two picks, including one that led to Denver's game-winning field goal.Despite those struggles, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald is not considering a change under center. "No, no," Macdonald said during a radio appearance when asked about a potential switch from Darnold to backup Drew Lock.Macdonald stated that the Seahawks have a starter-quality backup in Lock, but that the offense can find its way with Darnold under center.
"Sam's played great football for us this year the majority of the time," he said. "There's other times he needs to take care of the football but I think these are solutions we can find with Sam as our QB. I believe that."Lock played most of two games in place of Darnold (all but the first drive of the opener against the Patriots, and Week 2 against the Cardinals), completing 35 of 48 passes for 422 yards and four touchdowns. That performance was mostly out of line with what he's put on tape throughout his career, though, so it's not that surprising that the Seahawks aren't considering a change just yet. Even while he led the Seahawks to a Super Bowl victory, Darnold also struggled with turnovers last season, throwing 14 interceptions — but he was much more efficient in the passing game to make up for it. He completed 67.7% of his passes at an average of 8.2 yards per attempt. The Seahawks are breaking in a new offensive coordinator this year: Brian Fleury, who replaced the departed Klint Kubiak, now the head coach of the Raiders.
Macdonald acknowledged that Fleury has some things to figure out during the mini-bye before the Seahawks take on the undefeated Chiefs in Week 7. "Brian is well prepared. He's incredibly smart," Macdonald said, via Seattle Sports. "But as an offense, we need to really look at what we're doing, how we're doing it, what we're asking certain people to do. We need to look at all of those things right now."That process should probably involve looking at what they're asking Darnold to do and deciding exactly how it needs to be tweaked so he can rediscover some of what made him more effective for most of last season.

        One of college football's great rivalries takes center stage on Saturday night when No. 3 Miami welcomes Florida State for their traditional October clash. As usual, the game has ACC and national title race implications, though this season those conversations are focused far more on Miami, which finished last season as the national runner-up and is currently the heavy favorite to win the ACC in 2026. Things are far different for Florida State and embattled coach Mike Norvell, who entered the year facing serious job pressure and now risks falling to 3-4 on the season and 1-3 in ACC play if the Seminoles cannot pull a stunning upset. Wins against Miami in 2021, 2022 and 2023 were crucial building blocks of Norvell's eventual ACC Championship run, but now it's Mario Cristobal who has the chance to string together three straight wins in the series after the Hurricanes got the better of Florida State in 2024 and 2025. The return to Miami Gardens also spotlights what has become a notable home-field advantage for Miami in this recent run, as the Hurricanes are 15-1 at home since the start of the 2024 season, including that 36-14 win against the Seminoles in Hard Rock Stadium two years ago. Miami has been absolute rock stars in the ACC and the sport as a whole, continuing the momentum from the team's College Football Playoff run with eye-popping scores and stat-stuffing performances to start the 2026 season. Florida State hopes to provide more resistance than the average Miami opponent, but even that might not be enough to stop the ACC's most potent national title contender.
  Miami vs. Florida State: Need to know  A big stage for Darian Mensah's Heisman Trophy case: Miami quarterback Darian Mensah has been playing at an elite level all season, but the lopsided wins and predicted blowouts haven't given him the stage and audience that Saturday night's rivalry game will command. Miami may be in a far better place than Florida State this season, but this iconic rivalry will still bring the attention of Heisman Trophy voters to Hard Rock Stadium to see how Mensah performs under the pressure. Currently, he's one of just two FBS quarterbacks with 15-plus passing touchdowns and zero interceptions and boasts the best completion percentage (84.2%) and passer rating (212.2) in all of FBS. Mensah will still have a road trip to Notre Dame and a few other opportunities to shine in the spotlight, but Saturday night could prove to be the launching point for Mensah to push Jeremiah Smith in the Heisman conversation.   Florida State struggling against top teams: While Florida State has won three national championships and spent 72 weeks ranked No. 1 in the AP Top 25 poll throughout its history, the Seminoles have struggled against the best teams in recent years. As the Seminoles take aim at their rival from the South, they do so staring down a brutal losing streak against top-3 teams from the AP poll. Florida State has lost its last eight games against AP top-three teams, last winning in the BCS National Championship Game against Auburn at the end of the 2013 season. Another losing streak that Florida State can put to bed on Saturday night is a 12-game road losing streak against teams with any AP ranking, which stretches back to a 2016 win at Miami.  No one is beating teams like Miami is in 2026: The Hurricanes enter this annual rivalry checkpoint with one of the most dominant teams in the country, beating opponents by an average of 39.8 points per game. That's the largest points-per-game differential through five games in school history and is currently the largest among all FBS teams. Now, a skeptic would be quick to point out that a 70-point win against Florida A&M will do a lot to juice those averages, but it's the consistency with which Miami has been blitzing its opponents that stands out. Of Miami's five games, only one (a 33-20 win at Wake Forest) was decided by less than 28 points.
